2026-2027 SGi Executive Board Ushers in New Academic Year

Student leaders detail plans for upcoming semester.
Jack Bulik, News Editor • September 28, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:01
Instaread

As the school year begins, representatives on the Student Government Incorporated (SGi) Executive Board are preparing for the upcoming semester. 

President Andrew Fludd, Vice President Madison Yates, Secretary Ayman Mohammed, Press Secretary Kelysse Ochoteco, Treasurer Samantha Staromana and Senior Programming Coordinator Alliyah Sadiq are the students who were appointed to the executive board after student elections last spring. 

“Even though we have a new executive board, Ava Wilson is still a guiding light for us,” Fludd told The Torch during an exclusive sit-down interview with members of the executive board. 

Ava Wilson, the former student president, was elected alongside Fludd on the GLORY ticket in the 2025 SGi election. Since becoming President, Fludd says there has been a mentoring relationship between the two.

Ochoteco, the SGi Press Secretary, says she also feels a strong sense of mentorship from previous executive board members. 

“The previous E-board left such great building blocks for us that it makes our job so much easier to do what we do daily,” Ochoteco told The Torch.

During the SGi debate in April 2026, the now-appointed executive board ran together on the Vision ticket and promised better transparency between the administration, student government, and the student body. The ticket also made it clear they would create initiatives to “bolster campus culture.”

Student government maintains that one of the biggest issues facing St. John’s students is a lack of campus culture tying resident students to commuter students. 

“Students are feeling excluded; a lot of students don’t know about all these activities, committees and events SGi hosts here,” said Yates. 

“We are trying to get more exposure for those things; we’re trying to hear more about what students want, what the students need, and really just try to assist from there,” the Vice President continued.

One way that SGi is focused on helping the student body, Yates says, is by providing better access to feminine hygiene products. 

“We’re working with facilities right now, because right now it’s not accessible in every female restroom,” Yates said. 

“St. John’s students invested a lot of money into the school; we’re looking for some results to come back on those investments,” she concluded. 

SGi is also making significant progress on their digital storm card initiative, which is currently being implemented throughout the University’s Queens campus. 

SGi holds student senate meetings every Monday, inviting members of the student body to come speak their mind on important issues. The executive board invites anyone interested in attending student senate meetings to email SGi. 

Fludd, the student government president, compared the executive board’s plans for the upcoming year to a puzzle.

“We’re just collecting the pieces and starting to put them all together; by the end of the year – God willing, we will have our puzzle finished,” Fludd said. 

“My team has been vital in this process and ultimately, when we finish this puzzle, it’s all going to be because of the work that they’ve done.” 

For more info, visit the SGi Website.
